content.comment_body: I'm new to [product_name]. I'm trying to program the [product_name] to enable forward and reverse control of a 24V DC motor. Is it possible to achieve this using just two of the outputs in the program, or is an external relay required? Any advice is appreciated.
This can be done with four relay outputs, or with two if using a 48V three-wire power supply. However, the most reliable method is to use an external relay to control the motor direction.
My suggestion is to use the PLC as an H bridge with four relay outputs. You can find a helpful schematic on Wikipedia.

As mentioned earlier, it is possible, but ensure a timer is included so that when reversing direction, the relays have sufficient time to disengage. Otherwise, there is a risk of shorting the relay contacts and potentially damaging your PLC.

Thanks [user_name], I am currently using an external four-contact relay for the job. I hoped to accomplish it solely within the [product_name] to reduce components in my panel, but since I do not want to use all four outputs, I'll stick with the external relay. Thank you again.

I reviewed my wiring design many times before realizing the importance of proper timing. Each time the relays activated, I encountered a dead short, despite being confident in my wiring. Finally, I added a half-second delay to each input for opening and closing the relay, and everything worked properly. It's always interesting to learn firsthand how things operate. Thank you for confirming the necessity of these time delays. Thanks again, [user_name]
That's exactly why I mentioned the need for a delay—I've experienced the same issue before.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discussed controlling a DC motor's direction using [product_name] outputs. The primary concern was whether direct output control is feasible or if an external relay is necessary. Users highlighted practical difficulties such as limited outputs and timing delays causing short circuits, leading to a consensus that external relays and appropriate timing management are essential to avoid hardware damage.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hoped to control a DC motor's direction only with [product_name] outputs, minimizing additional components and avoiding the need for external relays.
